chunks: The 'FR' means the material is formulated to be self-extinguishing, so if it catches fire it stops burning when the flame is removed; it's rated V-0 in the UL 94 flammability test.
The '4' is just the grade number in the old NEMA classification of laminates, it doesn't mean four layers or four plies.
In practice, FR-4 is the standard PCB base material: woven fibreglass cloth impregnated with epoxy resin.
The glass gives it strength and stiffness, the epoxy bonds it and insulates, and a flame retardant, traditionally a brominated compound or now often a phosphorus-based halogen-free one, is added.
It's the flame-retardant version of an older grade called G-10. Typical properties: a dielectric constant of about 4. 2 to 4. 7, a loss tangent around 0.
02, a glass transition around 130 to 140 degrees Celsius for standard and 170 or more for high-Tg grades, and thermal conductivity of about 0. 3 watts/mK.
It dominates because it's cheap, strong, easy to drill, laminate and plate, and good enough electrically up to around a gigahertz. Above that we look at lower-loss materials."
